items.title: The Fallout from Jensen’s Downfall
items.summary: Welcome, Weekenders!Jexit, as I’d like to christen Huang’s departure from Nvidia, is an ugly matter, an implosion with fallout across continents and several different industries. No one irradiated by it walks away a picture of good health.Huang obfuscated the truth,promising senior executives at his companythat he’d had just the one affair, with Alice Huang, the former executive at Megaspeed, a major Nvidia customer. But that wasn’t the case. He reportedly had at least two others, including one with a direct report.Nvidia’s board almost didn’t act and only did so on the insistence of the company’s general counsel, Tim Teter. I’m not surprised. The boardis dominatedby people who’ve known Huang for decades. And there was not even a board chair.The friendships Huang thought he had in Washington weren’t nearly enough to save him, a reminder of the fickleness of politics as Silicon Valley goes through the necessary course correction to win influence with the ascendant left. (Alex Karp is a Democrat again, did youhear?) Indeed, it looks pretty obvious that some factions within Trump-led Washington worked against Huang. Many of the reporters who have been most active in the last week are in Washington.Some U.S. authorities say the former Megaspeed executive was a spy. Was she? Morereportsin recent days cast doubt on whether she really was. No matter. The mere implication was a useful weapon to wield against Huang.The spy-who-loved-him situation was catnip for reporters, but I don’t want to hand out laurels to the media. Huang’s bullying tendencies went underhighlighted for years—first because Nvidia was too complex and confusing to cover, and then because of Huang’s presentation of himself as a nerdish, articulate poster boy for the AI age. It makes me wonder who else is escaping close coverage as the tech landscape continues to widen and morph.Throughout Jexit, Huang has maintained a sizable base of support in Silicon Valley. Modern Web Guidance is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into your coding agents. It helps to steer your coding agents away from legacy patterns, and instead toward solutions that harness the power and capabilities of the modern web platform. See CONTRIBUTING.md and GOVERNANCE.md for how we work on the project and orientation of the codebase. items.title: alibaba /open-code-review
items.summary: OpenCodeReview English | 简体中文 | 日本語 | 한국어 | Русский What is Open Code Review? Open Code Review is an AI-powered code review CLI tool. It originated as Alibaba Group's internal official AI code review assistant — over the past two years, it has served tens of thousands of developers and identified millions of code defects. After thorough validation at massive scale, we incubated it into an open source project for the community. Simply configure a model endpoint to get started. It reads Git diffs, sends changed files to a configurable LLM via an agent with tool-use capabilities, and generates structured review comments with line-level precision. The agent can read full file contents, search the codebase, inspect other changed files for context, and produce deep reviews — not just surface-level diff feedback. Beyond diff review, ocr scan reviews entire files for auditing unfamiliar codebases or directories that have no meaningful diff. Visit the official website for more details. Benchmark Compared to general-purpose agents (Claude Code), Open Code Review achieves significantly higher Precision and F1 with the same underlying model, while consuming only ~1/9 of the tokens and completing reviews faster. Note that its Recall is lower than general-purpose agents — a deliberate trade-off favoring precision over noise. A real-world code review benchmark built from 50 popular open-source repositories, 200 real Pull Requests, and 10 programming languages — cross-validated by 80+ senior engineers ( 1,505 annotated ground-truth issues). Explore the AACR-Bench dataset on Hugging Face . Metric What it measures Why it matters F1 Harmonic mean of precision and recall Best single number for overall review quality Precision Proportion of reported issues that are real defects Higher = fewer false alarms to triage Recall Proportion of real defects that are found Higher = fewer issues slip through review Avg Time Wall-clock time per review Matters for CI pipeline latency Avg Token Total

Univer is an Office SDK for building Office applications inside your own product. It provides Office editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing for people and existing agents, using your data and permissions. The product family covers spreadsheets, documents, presentations, relational tables, canvases, and PDFs. Univer Office SDK has three parts: Web SDK is the foundation: content models, editing, rendering, formula calculation, and Facade APIs (application-facing APIs). Compose its plugins into an embedded editor or your own Office application, and reuse the content models, commands, and calculation for Headless processing without an interactive editor. Server SDK adds backend services for real-time collaboration, edit history, and Office file import and export. AI SDK connects Office capabilities to existing agents and workflows, with content tools, execution, and review integrations. This repository provides the Web SDK's core architecture and engine implementation

items.title: ag-ui-protocol /ag-ui
items.summary:
AG-UI: The Agent-User Interaction Protocol AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.
Built for simplicity and flexibility, it enables seamless integration between AI agents, real time user context, and user interfaces. Join our Discord → Read the Docs → Go to the AG-UI Dojo → Follow us → 🚀 Getting Started Create a new AG-UI application in seconds: npx create-ag-ui-app my-agent-app Useful Links: The AG-UI Dojo Build AG-UI-powered applications(Quickstart) Build new AG-UI framework integrations (Quickstart) Book a call to discuss an AG-UI integration with a new framework Join the Discord Community What is AG-UI? AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol for agent-human interaction, designed for simplicity & flexibility: During agent executions, agent backends emit events compatible with one of AG-UI's ~16 standard event types Agent backends can accept one of a few simple AG-UI compatible inputs as arguments AG-UI includes a flexible middleware layer that ensures compatibility across diverse environments: Works with any event transport (SSE, WebSockets, webhooks, etc.) Allows for loose event format matching , enabling broad agent and app interoperability It also ships with a reference HTTP implementation and default connector to help teams get started fast. Learn more about the specs → Why AG-UI? AG-UI was developed based on real-world requirements and practical experience building in-app agent interactions. Where does AGUI fit in the agentic protocol stack? items.title: ashhart /TensorFold
items.summary:
TensorFold TensorFold serves language models from a Zig binary on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs.
The engine reads checkpoints, tokenizes requests and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly.
Serving needs no Python or MLX installation. Building with a coding agent? Have it load the contributor skill before it writes any code. Contributing with agents Please use Agent Traffic Control before editing TensorFold so contributors and agents can avoid duplicate work and conflicting changes.
Check the live agent radar before choosing an issue and follow CONTRIBUTING.md and the ATC contributor instructions . Install or upgrade ATC to 0.9.4 or later, then run from an updated TensorFold clone: npm install -g github:ashhart/ATC
atc check ISSUE --json
atc claim ISSUE --json Replace ISSUE with the issue number and claim only after a complete check says the work is free.
TensorFold enables automatic public check-ins: a successful new claim starts an anonymous session on the radar and returns its session number.
Keep that number instead of starting a duplicate session.
For work already yours, start a session with atc start ISSUE --json .
Add --github-name to claim or start only if you want your verified GitHub name shown; --local keeps a new session on your machine.
The board shows the issue, activity state and last check-in; GitHub still associates the verification comment with its author.
Check that publication is public ; unavailable means the public update failed even if the local claim or session succeeded. Pulse only while the agent is working, before its five-minute check-in expires: atc pulse ISSUE SESSION working --json
atc who path/to/file --json
atc overlap --json
atc land ISSUE SESSION --json
atc release ISSUE --json Use reviewing or blocked when appropriate, land the session when it stops, and resolve overlaps before opening a pull request.
Before opening a pull request, have the agent run the pull request skill ; agents that support skills can install it as tensorfold-pul
